hook.line: Bogotá has uneven pavements, sudden rain and very fast motorbikes. Locals warn each other all day long, and they do it in about three words.
hook.en: Be careful when you cross. (to a friend)

examples.en: Be careful when you cross. (to a friend)
Be careful with the dog. (to a friend)
Be careful with the money. (to someone you address formally)
Be careful when you leave. (to you all)

examples.es: Está lloviendo, así que ten cuidado al manejar.
examples.en: It's raining, so be careful when you drive. (to a friend)

rule:
Warn with *cuidado* and say what to watch.

*Ten cuidado con* + a thing: *con el perro*.
*Ten cuidado al* + a verb: *al cruzar*, where English says "when crossing".

The first word follows who you talk to: *ten* (friend), *tenga* (*usted*), *tengan* (*ustedes*). Add *mucho* to push it: *ten mucho cuidado*.

*Ojo con* is the quick street version, literally "eye with": *¡Ojo con la cabeza!*

A reason first, then the warning, lands better.

options: Be careful with the dog. (to a friend)
Be careful with the money. (to a friend)
Be careful when you leave. (to a friend)
Be careful when you leave. (to you all)

options: It's raining, so be careful with the car.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (Be careful with the dog, to a friend): ___ cuidado con el perro. (*Ten* / *Tenga*)
Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (Be careful when you cross, to a friend): Ten cuidado ___ cruzar. (*con* / *al*)
yourTurn.why: Before a verb you need *al*; *con* goes before a noun.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (to someone you address as *usted*): Be careful with the money.
Type in Spanish (to several people): Be careful when you leave.
yourTurn.why: A group takes *tengan*, and *al* leads into the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Watch your head!
yourTurn.why: *Ojo con* is the quick warning, followed by the thing.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it stronger (to a friend): Ten cuidado al manejar.
yourTurn.why: *Mucho* goes between *ten* and *cuidado* to push the warning.

yourTurn.prompt: Put the reason first (to a friend): It's raining, so be careful when you drive.
yourTurn.answer: Está lloviendo, así que ten cuidado al manejar.
yourTurn.why: *Así que* links the reason to the warning.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The thing to watch out for follows *con*.
English uses "-ing"; Spanish uses *al* plus the infinitive.
A warning is a command, so *ten*, not the plain *tienes*.

personal: Think of someone about to do something risky or slippery. Warn them with *ten cuidado con…* or *ten cuidado al…*.
